candidate.answerReason: Every negative a satisfies \(|a|=-a\), and zero also satisfies it. A positive a cannot satisfy the equality because its absolute value is positive while -a is negative. Thus a must be nonpositive, choice C.

methods.label: Apply the absolute-value sign rule
methods.explanation: \(|a|=-a\) means that the absolute value of \(a\) equals its additive inverse. This holds only when \(a\leq0\), so \(a\) is nonpositive (note that \(a=0\) also satisfies the condition).
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 7 absolute-value sign rule, including its zero case.
